subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Assistive Technologies Overview
description: A micro-lesson that makes Assistive Technologies Overview usable.

hook.text: A user navigates your entire app using only their voice. Another uses only eye tracking. Both expect it to work.

buildup.text: Assistive technologies include screen readers, magnifiers, switch devices, voice control, and eye trackers.

discovery.text: Each technology interacts with the software differently, relying on semantic markup and proper focus management.

twist.text: Testing with one assistive technology is not enough. A screen reader works but keyboard navigation may not.

climax.text: Testing with three assistive technologies reveals issues that none of them individually would have exposed.

punchline.text: Know the tools your users use. Test with each of them.

quiz.question: Why test with multiple assistive technologies?
options: They all find the same issues
Each interacts differently and reveals unique problems
Only one is needed for compliance
